# LiteClip translation template (made by build.ps1, do not edit this file).
# To translate: copy this file, name it after your language (e.g. Spanish.txt), and write each
# translation after the "=>". Lines you leave empty stay in English. Keep {0}, {1} and \n as they are.

# ---- Editor.xaml
←  All clips =>

Show in folder => 
Copy => 
Copies the clip so you can paste it into Discord, a chat or a folder. => 
Fit for Discord => 
Makes a smaller copy of the selected part that fits Discord's upload limit, and copies it. => 
[  Set start => 
Set end  ] =>

Save trimmed clip => 
Exact cut => 
Exact: cuts on the exact frame (re-encodes on your GPU). Off: instant, but cuts to the nearest second. =>

# ---- Settings.xaml
Save settings => 
Clips and shortcuts => 
Clip lengths => 
Seconds, separated by commas (5 to 300). Use 2m for minutes. Add @shortcut to give a length its own key, e.g.  15, 30, 2m@Alt+F10 => 
Pause / resume => 
Mute microphone => 
Open LiteClip => 
Click a box and press the keys. Backspace clears it. => 
Video => 
Monitor => 
Resolution => 
Native is the lightest (all on the graphics card). Lower resolutions make smaller files but use some CPU. => 
Frame rate => 
Custom fps => 
Codec => 
H.264 plays everywhere. HEVC and AV1 make smaller files at the same quality (AV1 needs a newer graphics card and player). => 
Encoder => 
Quality => 
Best => 
Smallest => 
Show the mouse cursor in clips => 
Audio => 
Record game and system sound => 
Record my microphone => 
Microphone => 
Muted (records silence instead of your voice) => 
Keep game sound and microphone on separate tracks (for video editors) => 
Files => 
Clips folder => 
Change => 
File name => 
Use {app} (the game or app you were in), {date}, {time}, {length}. => 
Clean up old clips => 
Old clips go to the Recycle Bin, so you can still get them back. 0 = never. => 
Keep for => 
days    and at most => 
GB => 
The size the editor's Fit for Discord button aims for. 10 = Discord's free limit, 50 = Nitro Basic, 500 = Nitro. => 
MB => 
Look and feel => 
Show a pop-up when a clip is saved => 
Play a short sound when a clip is saved => 
Accent colour => 
Language => 
Add your own: copy lang\template.txt, fill in the translations, save it as lang\YourLanguage.txt. => 
Open language folder => 
Advanced => 
Start with Windows (runs quietly in the tray) => 
Run after saving => 
Optional command to run after each clip, {file} = the clip. Example:  explorer /select,{file}   Only put commands here that you trust. => 
Recording buffer folder => 
Where the rolling last-few-minutes recording is kept. Empty = Windows' temp folder. Pick a fast drive if you like. => 
Default => 
Encoder frames in memory (NVIDIA) => 
Each frame the graphics card keeps ready uses about 11 MB of RAM at 1440p. 1 = lightest, 4 = safest in very heavy games. => 
Custom encoder options => 
For FFmpeg experts. Replaces LiteClip's video encoder options, e.g.  -c:v hevc_nvenc -preset p7 -cq 20   Leave empty for normal. If recording stops working, empty this box. => 
FFmpeg command LiteClip runs right now => 
Nothing hidden: this is exactly how your screen and sound are being recorded. => 
Copy command => 
Portable mode => 
Open settings file => 
Reset everything => 
About => 
Remove LiteClip => 
Deletes everything LiteClip made on this PC: settings, thumbnails, temporary files, the recording buffer, the start-with-Windows shortcut and its program files. Your clips are kept. => 
Remove LiteClip from this PC =>

Where should LiteClip keep its rolling recording? =>

Command copied. => 
On. Settings, thumbnails and the recording buffer are kept inside LiteClip's own folder ({0}), so it leaves nothing on this PC and can run from a USB stick. => 
Off. Turn it on to carry LiteClip on a USB stick: settings, thumbnails and the recording buffer move into LiteClip's own folder. You can also turn it on by putting an empty file named portable.txt next to LiteClip.exe. =>
